chunks: Hafs narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The person who faints (loses consciousness) makes up what was missed from him.

key_terms.الْمَغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The person who faints or loses consciousness
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up / performs the qada

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up missed prayers or fasting for someone who fainted?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Hafs ibn al-Faraj narrates from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that a person who faints is exempt from making up the prayers missed during their unconsciousness, distinguishing this state from sleep or minor illness. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that *ghayb* (loss of consciousness) removes the obligation of *qada* for prayers, as the individual is considered absent from the realm of accountability during that interval. This contrasts with fasting, where the majority view in the school is that the fast remains valid but is not broken, or that makeup is required depending on the duration and cause, though this specific hadith focuses on the general exemption for missed acts.
